range.remark: Pss 91-94 complete, Ps 95 vv.1-8 (introductory essay treats Pss 95-100 as one liturgical group written for the dedication of the Zerubbabel temple; few textual notes so far). Continues -> next batch.

entries.mt: יֹשֵׁב בְּסֵתֶר עֶלְיוֹן בְּצֵל שַׁדַּי יִתְלוֹנָן
entries.note: A word (Olshausen, Hupfeld propose אשרי) must be supplied before ישב — otherwise the opening is unintelligible. Symmachus's participle for יתלונן fits better than the received text; ישב and התלונן both denote continual dwelling.
entries.flag: Symmachus's exact reading is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.emendation: יָקוּשׁ → יְקוּשִׁים (plural, ם absorbed by the next word); מִדֶּבֶר → מִדְּבַר ('word/matter', not 'plague')
entries.note: יקוש should be the plural יקושים, the ם absorbed by the following word. Since pestilence is not discussed until v.6, LXX correctly render this phrase 'from a matter/word of destruction' rather than 'from the plague of destruction' (cf. Ps 38:13 הוות).

entries.mt: יִפֹּל מִצִּדְּךָ אֶלֶף וּרְבָבָה מִימִינֶךָ אֵלֶיךָ לֹא יִגָּשׁ
entries.note: מצדך forms no contrast with מימינך; leg. משמאלך, since יד often specifically denotes the left hand. And statt the Niphal יגש leg. the Hiphil יגיש.

entries.mt: רַק בְּעֵינֶיךָ תַבִּיט וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶה
entries.note: רק בעיניך does not match the parallel half — 'only' what? The object must lie hidden in רק; since the word is rare and a stronger, plural term matching רשעים is needed, leg. שד עריצים: 'the ravage of the violent shall you see with your own eyes'.

entries.mt: כִּי־אַתָּה ה׳ מַחְסִי עֶלְיוֹן שַׂמְתָּ מְעוֹנֶךָ
entries.emendation: supply אָמַרְתָּ after כי אתה; מְעוֹנֶךָ → מְעוּזֶךָ
entries.note: After כי אתה supply אמרתה (Olshausen; the word may have been corrupted into אתה itself). And statt מעונך leg. מעוזך, as at Ps 90:1 and elsewhere.

entries.mt: וַתָּרֶם כִּרְאֵים קַרְנִי בַּלֹּתִי בְּשֶׁמֶן רַעֲנָן
entries.emendation: בַּלֹּתִי read as a form of מלא ('I am filled'); בְּשֶׁמֶן → כְּשֶׁמֶן
entries.note: LXX render as future (ὑψωθήσεται). בלתי, taken as from בלי, gives no proper sense; leg. instead a form meaning 'I am filled' (cf. Job 32:18's מלתי for ימלא, Job 36:11's יכלו leg. ימלאו). בשמן רענן, per Symmachus (ὡς ἐν ἐλαίῳ), should be כשמן: 'מלאתי כשמן רענן' — 'I am filled/anointed as with fresh oil'.

entries.mt: שְׁתוּלִים בְּבֵית ה׳ בְּחַצְרוֹת אֱלֹהֵינוּ יַפְרִיחוּ
entries.emendation: שְׁתוּלִים → הַשְּׁתוּלִים (ה absorbed by the ה of the next word, יַפְרִיחוּ)
entries.note: v.14 is plural while the subject of v.15 is singular — a different subject must be intended; leg. השתולים, the ה absorbed by the following word (Pesch. seems to reflect this reading, 'those planted'). Those planted in the Temple are the Levites.
Leg. אדיר ממשברי ים 'mightier than the breakers of the sea' (Dyserinck), rather than the received 'mighty are the breakers of the sea'.

entries.emendation: supply a word/clause such as נָוְךָ or וְשַׁבְתִּי (per Ps 23:6)
entries.note: עדתיך ('Thy testimonies, promises') נאמנו ('have proven true', perfect). The close 'ה׳ לארך ימים' is too short; vielleicht supply something like נוך, or ושבתי בביתך, as Ps 23:6 (ושבתי בבית ה׳ לארך ימים).
Precative form; leg. הופיעה (the ה absorbed, per Olshausen).

entries.emendation: reorder: אַלְמָנָה וִיתוֹמִים יַהֲרֹגוּ וְגֵר יְרַצֵּחוּ
entries.note: 'Widow and stranger' are never elsewhere paired — 'widows' pair with 'orphans'. The LXX reading is preferable, pairing אלמנה with יתומים and taking גר separately: אלמנה ויתומים יהרגו וגר ירצחו. These verses remain governed by v.3's עד מתי, hence the future sense.
נטע אזן ('who plants the ear') is striking; vielleicht leg. נטה 'who inclines, extends'.

entries.emendation: supply לֹא יָבִין at the close
entries.note: המלמד אדם דעת lacks its completion, namely לא יבין — thereby refuting the brazen claim (v.7) that 'the God of Jacob does not perceive'.
Leg. בתורתך statt ומתורתך.

entries.emendation: מִימֵי רָע → a reading built on מֵרֹעַ(?)
entries.note: מימי רע is unintelligible; the verb השקט is elsewhere used of water becoming calm (Isa 57:20, Jer 49:23), pointing to a different underlying construction here.
entries.flag: exact proposed reading garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.emendation: כִּי עַד עַד־צֶדֶק... (restore a repeated עד); supply יֵלֵכוּ at the close
entries.note: The verse has been misunderstood; a second עד seems to have dropped out: leg. עד כי עד צדיק ישוב משפט — 'until justice returns again to the righteous, until he obtains right'. And ואחריו כל ישרי לב requires the supplied verb ילכו, 'and after him shall walk all the upright of heart'.

entries.mt: מִי־יָקוּם לִי עִם־מְרֵעִים מִי־יִתְיַצֵּב לִי עִם־פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן
entries.emendation: supply אָמַרְתִּי at the opening; both instances of עִם → עַל
entries.note: At the opening supply אמרתי, 'I said to myself'; and leg. על מרעים and על פעלי און statt עם in both halves (per LXX, Symmachus).
LXX and Pesch. read the perfect סעדני, 'has supported me', rather than future.

entries.emendation: vocalize as a distinct Pa'el-type form, יְחַבְּרְךָ
entries.note: היחברך is without morphological analogy as usually parsed; Hebrew had, alongside the Piel, a parallel intensive pattern for this root (cf. הלל/התל; Arabic's Form III) — properly leg. יְחַבְּרְךָ, 'shall it ally itself with thee' (Olshausen).
This phrase, which lengthens the verse asymmetrically, is surely the fragment of a lost verse that made the transition from jubilation to reproof (Olshausen).
